import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

MAX_DRIVERS = 2

def design(feats):
    # Calculate effect sizes (mean difference) for all features
    effect_sizes = []
    for fid in feats.ids:
        col = feats.column(fid)
        y0 = feats.x[feats.y==0, col]
        y1 = feats.x[feats.y==1, col]
        effect_size = abs(np.mean(y1) - np.mean(y0))
        effect_sizes.append(effect_size)
    
    # Sort features by effect size
    sorted_indices = np.argsort(effect_sizes)[::-1]
    
    # Select top features by t-test to avoid near-duplicates
    selected_ids = []
    tstats = []
    
    for idx in sorted_indices:
        fid = feats.ids[idx]
        col = feats.column(fid)
        y0 = feats.x[feats.y==0, col]
        y1 = feats.x[feats.y==1, col]
        tstat, _ = stats.ttest_ind(y1, y0, equal_var=False)
        tstats.append(abs(tstat))
        
        # Check for near-duplicates (correlation >= 0.6)
        is_duplicate = False
        for selected_fid in selected_ids:
            selected_col = feats.column(selected_fid)
            corr = abs(np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, col], feats.x[:, selected_col])[0, 1])
            if corr >= 0.6:
                is_duplicate = True
                break
        
        if not is_duplicate:
            selected_ids.append(fid)
            if len(selected_ids) >= MAX_DRIVERS:
                break
    
    # Use top features as drivers
    drivers = tuple(selected_ids)
    
    # For columns, use only the drivers (keep model small)
    columns = list(drivers)
    
    # Products: only include interactions between top drivers
    products = []
    if len(drivers) >= 2:
        products = [(drivers[0], drivers[1])]
    
    # Loadings: simple effect sizes for drivers only
    loadings = {}
    for i, fid in enumerate(columns):
        loadings[fid] = effect_sizes[feats.column(fid)]
    
    return Design(drivers=drivers, columns=columns, products=products, loadings=loadings)
